datasets.title: Deconvolution of regulatory T cell heterogeneity identifies cycling precursors as conductors of immune escape during breast carcinoma progression
datasets.summary: Tumor-immune microenvironment is instrumental in shaping breast cancer tumor evolution. We previously identified an evolutionary bottleneck demarcating ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) from invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). How the microenvironment evolves during such transition remains elusive. We dissected, in parallel, single-cell composition of DCIS and IDC patients and rat tumors that faithfully recapitulate human breast cancer. We discovered T cell diversity distinguishing DCIS and IDC and a novel cycling Treg state occupying the pseudotime bifurcation between DCIS and IDC, preceding more activated Treg subtypes. Multiscale analysis of patient cohorts as part of HTAN Consortium established that cycling Treg predicts recurrence in low-grade DCIS. We proved cycling Treg as Treg progenitors critical for immune escape and demonstrated that OX40 agonism restored immunotherapeutic sensitivity, where responders displayed increased inflammatory CAF subtype heterogeneity. Our study thus established cycling Treg’s importance in preserving immune escape and underscored its prognostic value to stratify future recurrence.
datasets.overall_design: Dataset 1: Breast tissues of patients (DCIS, IDC) or healthy individuals (Normal) were subjected to tissue dissociation via collagenase 4/hyaluronidase and FACS sorted for immune, epithelial, myoepithelium, and stroma compartment based on lineage markers and later to droplet-based 10X scRNAseq (3'HTv3)/Illumina NovaSeq6000. Dataset 2: Outbred Sprague Dawley rats were injected with NMU carcinogen (50 mg/kg, twice, 7 days apart, starting at 40 days of age rat) to induce rat mammary tumors. Tissues from mammary glands (MG) of untreated rats or NMU-treated rats and progressing tumors from NMU-treated rats were dissociated by collagenase 4/hyaluronidase, FACS-sorted for immune, epithelium, and stroma fractions, and subjected to droplet based 10X scRNAseq (3'HTv3) pipeline and Illumina NovaSeq6000. Dataset 3: Rats treated with NMU as aboved were subjected to three immunotherapy regimens (+isotype control) right when NMU-tumors became palpable. The rats were treated by anti-OX40 agonist (every 48hr, 2.5 mg/kg, till sacrifice) or anti-PDL1 (every 7 days, 10.0 mg/kg, till sacrifice) or combination of anti-OX40 and anti-PDL1 or isotype (same dosage). Responding versus Non-Responding tumors of each treatment were dissociated by collagenase 4/hyaluronidased and selected for scRNAseq 10X pipeline (5'HTv2)/Illumina NovaSeq6000. Raw reads from dataset 1 were aligned with the human genome hg18 while reads from dataset2/3 were aligned with the Sprague Dawley rat reference genome (Rnor_6). Downstream analyses of Datasets 1-3 include basic filtering and quality control, removal of cell doublets, batch-effect control/integration, cell cluster identification, Milo neighborhood analysis, Trajectory inference by Monocle3, Coexpression hub analysis, GSEA, CellChat, etc.

datasets.title: Linking single cell genomes and transcriptomes at scale to decode breast cancer progression [scRNA-seq]
datasets._776385: 本数据由索臻生物科技(SOGEN)标注·免费共享欢迎转发·想要增量更新请加群·微信bioinformaticsboy
datasets.summary: Understanding the epithelial lineages of breast cancer and genotype-phenotype relationships requires direct measurements of the genome and transcriptome of the same single cells at scale. To achieve this, we developed wellDR-seq, the first high-genomic resolution, high-throughput method to simultaneously profile the genome and transcriptome of thousands of single cells in parallel. We profiled 33,646 single cells from 12 estrogen receptor-positive breast cancers, and identified ancestral subclones in multiple patients that showed a luminal hormone responsive lineage, indicating a potential cell-of-origin. Our data also identified sporadic copy number aberrations (CNAs) in the two luminal epithelial lineages and stromal cells. While gene expression was highly correlated with copy number in larger chromosome segments, our data reveals extensive variation at the single gene-level, reflecting differences in dosage-sensitive and dosage-insensitive genes. Overall, these data reveal the complex relationships between CNAs and gene expression in single cancer cells, improving our understanding of breast cancer progression.

datasets.title: Single-Cell Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Intratumoral Heterogeneity and Molecular Features in Breast Cancer
datasets._8b9e57: SOGEN·索臻生物科技·sogentech.com·增量更新与更多专题在群里·公众号医学僧的科研日记
datasets.summary: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is a nonobligate precursor of invasive breast cancer. Its biological features, particularly its intratumoral heterogeneity, remain obscure. Moreover, mechanism of lymph node metastasis is unclear. To address this deficiency, we performed single-cell transcriptome profiling of DCIS, invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and lymph node metastasis. Single-cell transcriptome analysis revealed that breast cancer exhibits intratumoral heterogeneity at the transcriptional level, defining specific functions, and that DCIS has similar heterogeneity to IDC.
datasets.overall_design: Single-cell transcriptome profiling from 13 human breast cancer tissues, 6 lymph node metastasis and 1 normal breast tissue. 13 breast cancer tissues include 7 ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and 6 invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). All cases of IDC are accompanied by lymph node metastasis, and lymph node metastasis was collected from each case of IDC.

datasets.title: Deconvolution of regulatory T cell heterogeneity identifies cycling precursors as conductors of immune escape during breast carcinoma progression
datasets.summary: Tumor-immune microenvironment is instrumental in shaping breast cancer tumor evolution. We previously identified an evolutionary bottleneck demarcating ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) from invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). How the microenvironment evolves during such transition remains elusive. We dissected, in parallel, single-cell composition of DCIS and IDC patients and rat tumors that faithfully recapitulate human breast cancer. We discovered T cell diversity distinguishing DCIS and IDC and a novel cycling Treg state occupying the pseudotime bifurcation between DCIS and IDC, preceding more activated Treg subtypes. Multiscale analysis of patient cohorts as part of HTAN Consortium established that cycling Treg predicts recurrence in low-grade DCIS. We proved cycling Treg as Treg progenitors critical for immune escape and demonstrated that OX40 agonism restored immunotherapeutic sensitivity, where responders displayed increased inflammatory CAF subtype heterogeneity. Our study thus established cycling Treg’s importance in preserving immune escape and underscored its prognostic value to stratify future recurrence.
datasets.overall_design: Dataset 5: Outbred Sprague Dawley rats were injected with NMU carcinogen (50 mg/kg, twice, 7 days apart, starting at 40 days of age rat) to induce rat mammary tumors. Tissues from mammary glands with microlesions (MG) and and progressing DCIS tumors from NMU-treated rats collected at different timepoints since NMU injection were dissociated by collagenase 4/hyaluronidase, and subjected to droplet based 10X scRNAseq (5'HTv3) pipeline and Illumina NovaSeq6000. Downstream analyses of Datasets 1-3 include basic filtering and quality control, removal of cell doublets, batch-effect control/integration, cell cluster identification, and module scoring.

datasets.title: Early dissemination and prognostic value of circulating tumor cells in ductal carcinoma in situ
datasets.summary: Widespread mammographic screening has resulted in a substantial increase in women diagnosed with Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS). To improve patient risk stratification, we investigate the prognostic value of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) as a biomarker for DCIS patients’ biological aggressiveness and as an indicator of early dissemination. Six enriched blood samples and six matching FFPE tissue samples are processed via single cell RNA sequencing.
datasets.overall_design: Blood samples are processed via a microfluidic device (the Labyrinth) to enrich CTCs. To meet 10X Genomics' minimum cell number requirement for sequencing, some white blood cells are supplemented into the initial sample. Hence, these data include six CTC enriched blood samples. In conjunction, FFPE tissues acquired from the same six patients are also processed for single cell RNA sequencing.

datasets.title: Molecular signatures of in-situ to invasive progression for basal-like breast cancers: An integrated mouse model and human tumor study [mouse]
datasets.summary: This study identifies progression in breast ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) as it progresses towards triple negative invasive breast cancer (TNBC).
datasets.overall_design: Single cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) and bulk RNA sequencing was performed on the C3Tag genetically engineered mouse model that forms human breast-like DCIS and TNBC. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on RNA harvested from 10 archival formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) pairs comprising of estrogen receptor (ER) positive (ER+) and ER- subsets of DCIS.
